notes:
I couldn't write any notes on Psalm 118 this time. My first attempt to open the source pages hit the tool's usage limit, and a retry was blocked, so I never read a single page.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, with a URL for each point. Without the pages, anything I wrote would come from memory, so I've left the notes out.

These are the pages I was trying to open, and the ones to start with when we try again:

- **Verse-by-verse (traditional reading):**
  - https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/psalm-118/
  - https://www.preceptaustin.org/psalm-118-commentary
  - https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/psalms/118.htm
  - https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/psalms/118.htm
  - https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/psalms/118.htm
- **Modern scholarship:** https://netbible.org/bible/Psalms+118 (translator notes, e.g. on "loving devotion" in vv. 1–4 and "save us" in v. 25)
- **Catholic and Orthodox:** https://www.newadvent.org/fathers/1801118.htm (Augustine's sermon on this psalm, which older Catholic Bibles number as Psalm 117)
- **Where traditions may differ, still to search:** vv. 22–23 (the rejected stone), v. 24 ("the day the LORD has made"), and vv. 25–26 ("Hosanna" and Palm Sunday). I'd look on gotquestions.org, ligonier.org, desiringgod.org, spurgeon.org, wesley.nnu.edu, 1517.org, oca.org and catholic.com. I'd also check what these sites say about popular prosperity-style uses of vv. 24–25.

If you ask again in a new message, I'll go through these one page at a time and write the verse-by-verse notes, with a URL after every point.
